text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy. Prepared for Reuters by Estonian News Agency ETA:
- The three Baltic presidents called in a joint statement on NATO to announce the names of countries to join the alliance in the second round of expansion.
- State inspector Hindrek Meri said former prime minister Tiit Vaehi had applied strong pressure on his office and delayed making public some of the alleged violations they had discovered.

- Prime Minister Mart Siimann warned yesterday that parliament's plan to adopt a declaration on the Estonian-Russian border agreement regarding the Tartu Peace Treaty may damage relations between the two countries.

- Leader of the Swedish representatives of the Estonia ferry Estonia commission Olof Forssberg resigned after admitting he had lied and withheld a document from the panel Families of the disaster victims demand setting up a new investigating body.
- Fuel firms yesterday increased the price of petrol by 15 cents and the price of diesel by 5 cents, saying the rise was due to increasing world oil prices.
- The crime rate can be lowered only by the joint efforts of law and order bodies and the people, the crime prevention council said.
- The financial police are to start an investigation over the actions of directors of the central prison in Tallinn, who are suspected of corruption.
- A high-level delegation of German businessmen will arrive in Estonia tomorrow to assess investment opportunities.
- Leaders of railway companies from CIS countries meet today in Tallinn to discuss technological and legal problems.
